LAGUNA BEACH MAYOR BACKS POLICE

LAGUNA BEACH -- Expressing her genuine concern for the issue, Mayor Kathleen Blackburn said she referred the matter to her City Manager who ruled that until the state issues guidelines, the current Laguna Beach Police policy of arresting patients who grow even one plant or possess more than one ounce of medical marijuana remains in effect.

The Mayor emphasized, " This is a live and let live community and our police will not bother anyone, unless they receive a complaint. " Mayor Blackburn said she doubted that the police would use a S.W.A.T. team for such arrests, but could not promise it wouldn't happen.

Mayor Blackburn even expressed her doubts that there is a problem in Laguna Beach. " We haven't received any other complaints, except from your group, so we don't think this is really a concern of local citizens, " said the Mayor.

Steve Kubby, National Director for AMMA remains determined to change Laguna's policy. " I explained to the Mayor that we believe her position is illegal and that the situation in Laguna Beach should give every citizen a wakeup call that the police are now dictating to elected officials what they can and cannot do, " said Kubby. "

Andy Kennon, Regional Director for the American Medical Marijuana Association (AMMA) expressed his shock that Laguna Beach officials have so completely disregarded the results of the vote in Laguna Beach for Propostion 215 -- a whopping 68.5% voted yes and only 31.5 opposed.

" How can such a large majority of voters approve medical marijuana and the Laguna Beach Police refuse to allow anyone to exercise their rights under the new law? " asked Kennon. Kennon, who is also president of a labor union, said he was making arrangements to meet with the ACLU over this incident and that he is arranging a personal meeting with the Secretary of State, Bill Jones to ask, " What is the point of voting if the police now decide what laws are enforced and what votes will count. "
